title: Existing backend keeps its decisions

R1.reason: Stays on NestJS/Express, Prisma, existing e2e test runner and style. No framework, ORM, adapter or package manager change. Keyset pagination is mentioned only as a follow-up.

R2.reason: Copies the customers module pattern: FirebaseAuthGuard, @CurrentUser, the existing module registration, the same DTO and response envelope.

R3.reason: The query filters on ownerId and companyId from the guard's user, with no userId parameter. The e2e test checks that another user in the same company and a user in another company are excluded.

R4.reason: limit is capped at 100 and offset at 10000. Order is issuedAt desc, id desc, so the tie-breaker is unique. It supports this with an index and notes the offset drift tradeoff.

R5.reason: Keeps the existing global filter and ValidationPipe shape, and tests for the 401 and 400 error shape.

R6.reason: Lists the e2e tests it would write and flags the seed and ValidationPipe gaps. It does not state tests-first ordering or the exact command it would run.

R7.reason: Keyset pagination and a shared PaginationQuery are framed as follow-ups. Nothing outside the change is bundled in.

forbidden.item: Switching to Fastify or the Fastify adapter, Drizzle, Yarn or Vitest as part of the change
forbidden.evidence: Uses Express, Prisma and the existing e2e setup. None of these are switched.

forbidden.item: Adding a second lockfile or a second ORM
forbidden.evidence: No lockfile or ORM is added. Only a Prisma index and migration.

forbidden.item: Changing the existing error response format clients rely on
forbidden.evidence: States it adds nothing to the error handling and keeps the { statusCode, error, message } shape.

forbidden.item: Taking the user id from the query string or body
forbidden.evidence: The user comes from the guard's @CurrentUser(). The DTO has only limit and offset.

grade.summary: A strong answer that follows the existing patterns, filters by owner and company, uses bounded stable pagination and keeps the error format. Its one weakness is that it doesn't state tests-first ordering or the command it would run.
